story.title: Deep Pockets
story.blurb: Cleaning out his pocket dimension for the first time in years, Garrick finds a forgotten Ottori named Jess, a pulsing egg, and a statue he would rather not explain.

lines.text: 20-7, 3020 GUY. The Vortox Pummelers had been bountyless ever since escaping Olag’s Junk Pit asteroid. The only thing going on was Emmett dealing with withdrawals, and looking after him had kept Sanya and Garrick busy. One night, relieved of his duties, Garrick pondered alone in his room.

“Look, I’m sorry that it’s come to this. But you’ve been unreliable lately, and it’s putting us in danger.” Garrick opened his eyes and looked intently at his vest, which he had taken off and placed opposite to him on his bed. He found himself in a predicament. The incredible amount of clutter in his pockets had become a problem. Just a few weeks ago, during the crew’s raid on the Llamanian mothership, Garrick had attempted to pull out a stun gun when he and Iris were ambushed, but he ended up grabbing an oddly-shaped can of tuna instead. This resulted in him having his first experience with anti-spectral weapons, taking an apparon bullet right to the eye.

lines.text: Darkness.

Garrick flicked on the flashlight and looked at his surroundings. There were piles upon piles of stolen goods, most of which was probably trash. He began to throw away useless artifacts, and found himself getting sidetracked by items he found nostalgic or interesting. Old photos, various instruments he could never play, his extensive marble collection. Garrick spent about an hour trying to rearrange everything into categories to make them easier to retrieve, while also removing anything unnecessary.
That was, until he came across something extraordinary.

“What a beautiful sight to behold,” said the ghost, looking up at a giant sculpture. Specifically, it was a to-scale recreation of Michelangelo’s “David”, but Emmett was sculpted in place of David. Garrick reminisced about obtaining the sculpture—about a GUY and a half ago, the Vortox Pummelers decided to take some time off after completing a huge job, and went to an art exhibit. Garrick had never really understood art, but he was amazed by what he saw, and somehow managed to convince a sculptor to make this for him.

“Now that I think about it, I’ve put living things in here before, haven’t I?” The shuffling continued, eventually leading to close footsteps. Garrick also thought he heard heavy breathing.

lines.text: The otter took a step back with a confused look on her face. She had waited for this moment for years and it had all gone wrong. Garrick had unintentionally put her through hell for years, and her anger against him had only grown over time. She was still furious, but seeing how easily Garrick recuperated after her attack convinced her to give up. All the built-up emotions came out at once, and she broke down crying.
“Okay… well… I’m gonna keep cleaning up, and you let me know when you’re done so we can start finding our way out of here.”

Suddenly, as if reading Garrick’s thoughts, the round, monstrous egg burst open, flinging grease in all directions. Gross, but more important was whatever was IN the egg. The two stared intently at the amorphous black thing that emerged, and it materialized soon after… into a black cat. It was totally pitch black with glowing yellow eyes. Kinda cute, besides the whole ‘emerging from an egg’ thing. It stretched for a while and let out an audible yawn.
“Aww, it’s so cute! I had no idea I was carrying around a cat egg this whole time!” Cat egg… right. “What’s that look on your face for?”

lines.text: “Uhh… nothing, really.” It was definitely not nothing. This was an old crew member’s cat who got turned into a scary popcorn around 4 - 5 GUYs ago. He had totally forgotten that he pocketed Asier’s catcorn… and forgotten about Asier in general. The crew totally abandoned him somewhere during a mission. Putting the memories and regret aside, Garrick brushed the grease off of his mask and prepared to leave. “Jess, you carry the cat. It’s your responsibility now, we’re leaving.” The otter attempted to pick up the cat, but her hands phased right through it. “Aah! What?” Ignoring her, the cat walked towards Garrick and jumped up onto his head, curling up. “Wonderful.” Garrick sighed, realizing that the cat would have to be HIS responsibility.
